questions.q: Why do intermediate models exist between staging and marts?
options: So marts models don't have to cram every join and complex transformation into one unreadable file
Because staging models are not allowed to have any downstream dependents
Because dbt requires exactly three layers in every project
To store raw, unrenamed source data permanently
questions.explain: Intermediate models break a marts-model's ten-plus joins and complex logic into purpose-built, independently understandable steps.

questions.q: What does 're-graining' mean in the context of intermediate models?
options: Changing the level of detail data lives at, such as fanning an orders table out to the order_items grain
Renaming a column to be more consistent
Converting a source's raw text into a real timestamp
Deleting duplicate rows from a source table
questions.explain: Re-graining is one of the three real jobs of an intermediate model — changing detail level, like orders to order line items.

questions.q: What does the design principle 'narrow the DAG, widen the tables' actually warn against?
options: An intermediate model with many different downstream outputs, which signals it's doing too many unrelated things
Having more than one staging model in a project
Materializing a mart as a table instead of a view
Using the ref() function more than once in a model
questions.explain: Many inputs into an intermediate model is good; many different outputs depending on it for different reasons is the warning sign.

questions.q: How are intermediate models materialized by default, and why?
options: Ephemeral — interpolated into downstream queries at run time, never built as their own warehouse object
As permanent tables, so BI tools can query them directly
As snapshots, to track how the intermediate logic changes over time
They cannot be materialized at all in dbt
questions.explain: Ephemeral is the default, keeping intermediate models out of the warehouse and out of any BI tool's table picker.

questions.q: How are intermediate models organized and named, and how does that differ from staging?
options: By business grouping (e.g. intermediate/finance/), using an int_[entity]s_[verb]s.sql verb-first naming pattern — unlike staging, which organizes by source system
Alphabetically, with no folder structure at all
By the BI tool that will eventually consume them
Exactly the same way as staging models, source-system by source-system
questions.explain: By this layer data has started to mean something to the business, not just the source system, so organization shifts to business grouping.
